# 2006A Question 7 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Briefly outline**]{.task-verb} the pharmacology of naloxone.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Briefly outline**]{.task-verb} pharmaceutics, kinetics and dynamics, linking high clearance and short duration to clinical use and recurrence of opioid effects. Include important adverse effects.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Pharmaceutics

### Administration and Pharmacokinetics

### Competitive Opioid Antagonism

### Clinical Applications and Adverse Effects
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**73 %** of candidates passed this question.

The majority of answers were well organized. The main points to include were:

- Pharmaceutics
- Pharmacokinetics
  - IV and IM administration
  - High clearance, short half life
  - High lipid solubility
  - Clinical implications
- Pharmacodynamics
  - Competitive mu opioid receptor antagonist
  - Clinical applications
  - Adverse effects

Common problems included; lack of organization, failure to discuss the important pharmacokinetic properties or the potential serious adverse effects of naloxone.
:::
